reason: Attacked on the obvious ground and it held. The dragons passage is a notorious misattribution magnet, but the trap is a DIFFERENT sentence: “our deepest fears are like dragons guarding our deepest treasure”, which is Sogyal Rinpoche's 1992 paraphrase in The Tibetan Book of Living and Dying, footnoted to p. 92 of Mitchell and not present there, then hardened into quotation marks by Dawna Markova in 1994. The line under review is not that sentence. Three independent checks agree that the “beauty and courage” English is Stephen Mitchell's 1984 rendering and that the dragons passage does sit on p. 92 of that translation: a quote-verification publisher states outright that the wording people love, the one with beauty and courage in it, is Mitchell's from 1984 and still in copyright to him; the same page confirms that the dragons are on p. 92; and a widely reproduced quotation record carries the sentence in exactly this form. The competing renderings are visibly different and rule themselves out: Norton has “only waiting to see us once beautiful and brave”, Maurer at rilkepoetry.com has “waiting for us to show a little beauty and courage”. Locator holds: the eighth letter, to Franz Xaver Kappus, from Borgeby gård, Flädie, Sweden, 12 August 1904, confirmed on two sites. Attribution, scope (letter of 1904, translation 1984, both pre-2000), tag (Correspondence, and it is a letter), publishability and the theme of courage all hold. shipped.js: not shipped, no near match, Rilke stands at two of three for the year with months 1 and 3, so a third line in July is allowed and does not double him in a month. Source line leads with the name, has no dash of any kind, no straight quote, 119 characters. Residual, not enough to refute: I did not open Mitchell's printed page, so the exact commas of “act, just once, with beauty and courage” rest on secondary attestation rather than the edition itself, and the heading is printed “Borgeby gård, Flädie, Sweden” where the source line abbreviates to “Borgeby gård”.
